ops.title: Operational facts for driving the tart macOS guests (bluebubbles) and running GPU spikes — SSH is off, cloning a live tailscale VM contends
ops.body:
The **bluebubbles macOS guest** has **OpenSSH (port 22) DISABLED** — reach it via **`tailscale ssh root@bluebubbles` / `admin@bluebubbles`** (once on the tailnet) or **VNC (5900)** on its vmnet IP. Admin user is `admin`; the login password is the 32-char generated value in the yclaw keychain (`yclaw-bluebubbles-admin-pass`, `uv run yclaw secret read bluebubbles-admin-pass`) — NOT the literal `bluebubbles` (that older note was wrong).

**State as of 2026-07-05:** bluebubbles is ON the tailnet (`100.82.87.19`, `tag:bluebubbles`), joined by typing `tailscale up --authkey <minted> --ssh --hostname bluebubbles --advertise-tags=tag:bluebubbles` directly in a VNC-driven Terminal (SSH/tailnet were down; driving VNC input has hard quirks — see [[bluebubbles-vnc-input-quirks]]). Live autologin was fixed by writing `/etc/kcpassword` directly (Apple XOR cipher) + `autoLoginUser=admin` — `sysadminctl -autologin set` hit `SACSetAutoLoginPassword error:22` over SSH. **BlueBubbles SERVER app is NOT installed** (`/Applications/BlueBubbles.app` absent, no `bluebubbles-server` config dir) though Messages/iMessage is signed in (active `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`). So `hermes-agent` stays `activating` — its `waitForBlueBubbles` gate probes `https://bluebubbles.<tailnet>/api/v1/server/info`, which won't answer until BlueBubbles is installed + `tailscale serve --https=443 1234`. Installing it is human-gated (app install + Private-API helper + password config).

**Do NOT clone a running tart VM that is a tailscale node and boot the clone on a routable network.** Tried it for a GPU spike (`tart clone bluebubbles metal-spike`; `tart run --no-graphics`): the clone boots with the SAME tailscale node key, transiently contends with the live node, and the live bluebubbles' tailnet REST blipped `200 → 000`. It self-healed within seconds once the clone was stopped+deleted, but it IS a real production blip. `--net-host`/`--net-softnet` (which would isolate it) need root/passwordless-sudo, which this shell lacks (`sudo -n` = NO).

**For GPU/MLX feasibility spikes**, use a FRESH cirruslabs base image instead: `tart pull ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-tahoe-base:latest` (~27 GB compressed; admin/admin, SSH enabled, NO tailscale identity → NAT is safe + fully scriptable). Host `powermetrics` needs root (unavailable), so measure GPU engagement from INSIDE the guest (admin sudo) plus tok/s as the proxy. Host is M4 Max / 128 GB / macOS 26.4.1.

**GPU-in-guest GATE: PASSED (Jun 2026).** In a tart macOS 26.5 guest (the cached `macos-tahoe-base`), `mlx.core.default_device()` → `Device(gpu, 0)`; fp32 4096³ matmul ≈ **4941 GFLOPS** (~host-parity for M4 Max; CPU-only would be ~100-300); `mlx_lm generate` on Qwen3-0.6B-4bit ≈ **452 tok/s**. So Metal compute works at full speed in an Apple Virtualization guest — the metal-VM architecture (Phase 2) is viable. Note: `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` is EMPTY in a `--no-graphics` guest (no display device) yet Metal compute still works — don't use it as the GPU check; use MLX's device. See [[secret-handling-and-state-store]].
